Article Title: 55 Indians still in Russian army: New Delhi presses Moscow at key meet, take action against agents
Article Text:
India continues efforts to secure the return of nationals serving in the Russian army (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Around 140 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian army have been discharged, while India is seeking information on the whereabouts of 55 others reportedly serving in the Russian armed forces, according to the details from India-Russia consultative committee meeting as cited by news agency ANI.New Delhi has engaged with Russian authorities for the early discharge of all such individuals."The government of India engaged with Russian authorities, including at the highest levels, for the early discharge of all such individuals. So far, around 140 Indian nationals have been discharged. Indian side is in touch with Russian authorities for the whereabouts of 55 Indian nationals who are reportedly in the Russian Army. Strong action being taken by the Indian law enforcement authorities against unscrupulous agents," the update from the meeting said.The latest figures are broadly in line with those shared by foreign secretary Vikram Misri last month. At the time, Misri said 139 of the 227 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian armed forces had been discharged, while 51 had died.Misri said the issue had been raised with Russia “at various levels on various occasions”.“At last count, we had information about 227 Indian nationals who had been recruited into the Russian army,” Misri had said. “Out of that, we have information that 139 of our nationals have been discharged from the army. And unfortunately, of course, we have information also about 51 people who have perished so far.”Misri had said India remained in constant discussions with Moscow to secure the early discharge and repatriation of those still serving.
Article Summary: New Delhi has engaged with Russian authorities for the early discharge of all such individuals. India is seeking information on the whereabouts of 55 others reportedly serving in the Russian armed forces. The latest figures are broadly in line with those shared by foreign secretary Vikram Misri last month.

Article Title: FSSAI steps up festive food crackdown as adulteration raids intensify
Article Text:
The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.

NEW DELHI: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement across the country, with thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in Delhi-NCR. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has now directed all states and Union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali.In Delhi alone, food safety teams have destroyed more than 4,100 kg of suspected adulterated khoya and paneer during enforcement action last month, while samples of khoya, paneer, chhena and ghee are being collected from markets for testing.In neighbouring Mewat, officials have seized and destroyed more than 10,000 kg of adulterated paneer in last months, with around 50 raids conducted in areas identified as production hubs. Officials said the supply chain extends to Jaipur, Mathura, Gurugram, Faridabad and Delhi, raising concerns over the movement of adulterated paneer into the wider National Capital Region.Against this backdrop, FSSAI on September 29 directed food safety authorities across the country to step up surveillance and enforcement against adulterated, counterfeit and unsafe food products during the festive season.The regulator has specifically identified milk and milk products, sweets, snacks and savouries, edible oil, beverages and ghee for heightened scrutiny.States have been asked to conduct inspections and sampling at identified hotspots and sensitive locations. The directive also asks authorities to record inspection, sampling and outcome data on the Food Safety Compliance System (FoSCoS) and Food Safety Compliance through Regular Inspection and Sampling of Food (FoSCoRIS) on a real-time basis.The national directive also allows states to focus on products specific to local consumption patterns, including kuttu atta and singhada atta in northern and western regions.
Article Summary: With festive demand for sweets and milk products rising, food safety authorities have stepped up enforcement across the country. Thousands of kilograms of suspected adulterated food already seized or destroyed in Delhi-NCR. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has directed all states and Union territories to intensify inspections and sampling during Navratri and Diwali.

Article Title: After Chandrayaan-3, ICMR asks scientists to attempt the ‘impossible’ in healthcare
Article Text:
Rs 8 crore on offer for health innovations that have never been tried anywhere in the world (Representativ e imaeg

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to successfully land near the Moon’s south polar region, the government is now asking scientists to attempt something equally audacious in healthcare: develop something the world has never tried before.The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched its “First in the World Challenge”, inviting researchers to develop breakthrough vaccines, drugs, therapeutics, diagnostics and other health technologies that have never been thought of, tested or tried anywhere in the world.The initiative will offer up to Rs 8 crore for a single project, depending on how advanced the proposed innovation is. ICMR describes it as a high-risk, high-reward programme, acknowledging that some projects may fail but saying successful ones could bring about a major change in healthcare.The grants will be released in stages: up to Rs 1 crore for proof-of-concept, Rs 4 crore for prototypes and Rs 8 crore for final products or implementation models. Funding will be linked to deliverables, with ICMR reviewing each stage before approving the next.The opportunity is open beyond ICMR scientists. Researchers from government medical colleges, Institutes of National Importance, universities, recognised research laboratories and eligible NGOs can apply.Indian startups, micro, small and medium enterprises and industry are also eligible.The scheme targets genuinely new health technologies, not incremental improvements. ICMR will first check whether a proposal is truly “first in the world”, followed by assessment of its relevance and potential impact by a panel of experts, innovators, policymakers and scientists.The programme aims to take innovations from the lab to deployment, requiring researchers to detail regulatory, validation, commercialisation and technology-transfer plans, as well as demonstrate the technology’s clinical need, advantages over existing options and readiness for deployment.Applications will open on October 7 and close on November 30, with results due on December 31. Each proposal must include at least one co-principal investigator from the principal investigator’s institution. ICMR says the initiative is willing to back high-risk ideas with uncertain outcomes but potentially transformative gains, in pursuit of breakthroughs no one has achieved before.
Article Summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has launched its ‘First in the World Challenge’ The initiative will offer up to Rs 8 crore for a single project, depending on how advanced the proposed innovation is. ICMR describes it as a high-risk, high-reward programme.

Article Title: 'Had productive conversation': PM Modi speaks with US President Trump on trade, defence, energy
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday said that he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump and reviewed bilateral cooperation between New Delhi and Washington in various sectors.In a social media post on X, PM Modi said the leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward."Had a productive conversation with President Trump. We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward," PM Modi said."We also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security," he added.The two leaders agreed to remain in touch as both sides continue to deepen the strategic partnership.This comes days after Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran and giving his administration expanded powers to penalise countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, including India.The legislation is particularly significant for India because it gives Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas.India and China are among the major purchasers of Russian crude.Earlier in September, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislation's potential impact on the US-India relationship."This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side," the ministry had said.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi says he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump. The two leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward. This comes days after Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday launched “ Satyagraha ," a digital platform aimed at consolidating information on various issue-based protests taking place across the country.The website was launched a day after the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi , whose philosophy of “Satyagraha” — peaceful resistance for truth — Rahul Gandhi invoked.In a post on X, the Raebareli MP noted that protesters can submit details about their causes, find similar movements across the country through an interactive map and seek direct support.“People across the country are fighting for their rights and often fighting alone. Gen Z, students, farmers, tribals, Dalits, women — every struggle has its own story. But the voice that rises alone often gets suppressed. ‘Satyagraha’ is an initiative to bring these voices together on a map. Bapu taught us this; truth is the greatest weapon. But an even greater weapon is standing together with truth in unity. If you’re also fighting against any injustice, share your story. It will take two minutes,” Rahul Gandhi said.“Your story will appear on the map. You’ll see who else is fighting like you. And I’ll do whatever I can, in Parliament, on the streets, by writing letters, standing with you wherever I’m needed, as the Leader of the Opposition; this is my responsibility,” the former Congress president added.In a video accompanying the post, Rahul Gandhi asserted that as the leader of opposition, it was his “responsibility” to consolidate information about protests across the country in one place.“Protests are taking place in every corner of the country. Someone is speaking about students, someone is speaking about women, someone is protesting against price rise, so there are lakhs of different protests happening across the country. I am the Leader of Opposition, and I wanted us to consolidate the information about all these protests in one place. That is why we have launched the Satyagraha website for you.Whatever your protest may be, big or small, enter your name, the name of your group, and detail what the protest is about. And if we can help you, or if you seek help from us, we will gladly support you,” Rahul Gandhi said.More than 150 submissions had already been made, with education accounting for the highest number—36.Student protests have taken place in several states over paper leaks. In July, then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned amid youth-led protests following the NEET-UG paper leak. The demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, Delhi’s designated protest site, were organised by the youth outfit Cockroach Janta Party.
Article Summary: Congress MP and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday launched “ Satyagraha," a digital platform aimed at consolidating information on various issue-based protests. The website was launched a day after the 157th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

Article Title: Himachal implements mandatory dress code for teachers in government CBSE schools
Article Text:
The dress code has been formulated as per the climatic conditions of Himachal Pradesh (Photo: ANI).

Himachal Pradesh implemented a mandatory dress code for teachers across 148 government CBSE schools on Thursday, attempting to create a more organised and professional learning environment.A notice dated September 10 explained that the prescribed dress code has been formulated "keeping in view the professional requirements of the teaching profession, uniformity in appearance and the climatic conditions of Himachal Pradesh."The dress code's colour palette includes light lilac, lilac purple and navy blue, with black prescribed for footwear and other specified accessories.The prescribed dress code offers female teachers three alternatives: a saree with a blazer, a kurta/kameez with pants, a plazo or salwar and a blazer, and a shirt and blazer with pants and a tie. For male teachers, however, only a single formal combination has been laid down: shirt with a tie, pants, and a blazer.According to the notice, the dress code is mandatory and will apply to all teachers, including principals, without exception, regardless of how they were recruited or engaged. This includes teachers whose services are being availed on an outsourced basis, for the time being.Reasonable adjustments may be allowed with the approval of the head of the institution in cases of medical necessity, disability or pregnancy.The state government also plans to open 100 new CBSE schools from the coming academic session, while roughly 2,000 teaching posts in CBSE schools have already been filled, PTI reported.To reinforce accountability, a system that logs teachers' attendance three times a day is also being brought in.Director of school education, Ashish Kohli, said the reforms had made a positive difference to the education sector, placing greater importance on quality education, equal opportunities, accountability and learning centred on students. He added that this had made Himachal Pradesh a role model for education reforms.

Indian intelligence and law enforcement agencies have secured the deportation of notorious narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye, striking a major blow against international illicit drug networks operating across foreign borders.Union home minister Amit Shah said in a post on X that Modi govt had achieved a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye."Obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Navab Virk, he had continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from Afghanistan. Article Title: India’s great hunt for oil: Inside the ₹84,000-crore Samudra Manthan mission
Article Text:
India is pushing for increased exploration of offshore oil and gas resources in various basins.

India's offshore oil hunt

From PM Modi's 2025 announcement to

Samudra Manthan

Where Rs 84,084 crore will go

Mahanadi is the immediate deepwater test

Mahanadi and Andaman in focus

Andaman is the frontier hunt

Krishna-Godavari is pushing deeper

Cauvery adds another deepwater target

The western offshore areas are also part of the plan

From geological potential to actual production

From discovery to production

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is taking its search for oil and natural gas deeper into the sea.The focus is now spread across the Mahanadi basin off Odisha, the frontier waters of the Andaman-Nicobar region, and deeper sections of the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins. The government's latest assessment puts the hydrocarbon potential of India's eastern and western offshore basins at more than 5,600 million metric tonnes of oil equivalent (MMTOE), with water depths extending to 3,000 metres.Recent discoveries in the Cauvery, Mahanadi and Andaman basins have strengthened the case for expanding offshore exploration.The push comes as India remains heavily dependent on imported energy. India is the world's third-largest consumer of crude oil and has an annual crude oil import bill of nearly $144 billion, or about ₹13 lakh crore, according to the government.There is another problem. Existing oil and gas fields naturally decline by around 6 to 7 percent each year. New discoveries are therefore essential to sustain domestic production.The current push is the latest stage of a decade-long effort to reshape India's upstream oil and gas sector.The government introduced the Hydrocarbon Exploration and Licensing Policy (HELP) in 2016 and launched the Open Acreage Licensing Programme (OALP). It also moved from Production Sharing Contracts to Revenue Sharing Contracts and expanded the National Data Repository.The government subsequently opened almost 99 percent of the offshore areas earlier classified as "No-Go" for exploration. This made more than one million square kilometres of India's Exclusive Economic Zone available for exploration.Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave the next phase a mission-mode identity in his Independence Day address on August 15, 2025.Calling the effort a modern-day "Samudra Manthan", PM Modi said India would work in mission mode to find oil and gas reserves beneath the sea. He also announced the National Deep Water Exploration Mission.On July 31, 2026, the Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan, the National Offshore Exploration Scheme. The central sector scheme, under the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, has an outlay of ₹84,084 crore through financial year 2030-31.The scheme allocates ₹28,534 crore for offshore seismic data acquisition, processing and interpretation, and ₹43,200 crore for 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration wells.The government will support up to 50 percent of eligible drilling costs, subject to a ceiling of ₹675 crore per well. The scheme also provides ₹10,000 crore for common offshore infrastructure, ₹2,000 crore for oil and gas manufacturing and services zones, and ₹350 crore for monitoring and support activities.But the real test of Samudra Manthan lies beneath the numbers.It is about where India is drilling, what it has already found, and whether those discoveries can eventually become producing fields.The Mahanadi Offshore Basin off Odisha is one of the most important tests of India's deepwater strategy.On July 25, Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri marked the start of drilling of MN-DWN18-1-HD, the first appraisal well in the Mahanadi Offshore Basin.It is the first of four planned deepwater wells intended to systematically evaluate the basin, which the government considers one of India's most prospective offshore areas.An appraisal well is drilled to determine the quality and commercial potential of an existing hydrocarbon discovery. The four-well programme is therefore an important step beyond seismic interpretation. It is designed to establish how significant the basin's discoveries could actually be.Government records show that ONGC had already made two gas discoveries in the Mahanadi offshore area after the opening of the former No-Go zones. One of these was in a block where 94 percent of the area had earlier been classified as No-Go.But finding hydrocarbons is only the first step.The Mahanadi basin also highlights why Samudra Manthan includes a major infrastructure component. The government says several offshore discoveries remain undeveloped because production and evacuation costs are too high, particularly in the Mahanadi and Kutch basins.The scheme's ₹10,000 crore common infrastructure component is aimed at tackling that problem.Further east, the Andaman-Nicobar offshore basin represents a more frontier form of exploration.The government's 2017 Hydrocarbon Resource Assessment Study estimated hydrocarbon resources in the Andaman-Nicobar basin at 371 MMTOE. Following HELP, four blocks covering approximately 23,261 square kilometres were allocated for oil and gas exploration. Government data says exploration in those blocks generated 8,501 line kilometres of 2D seismic data, 3,270 square kilometres of 3D seismic data and three drilled wells.Another four blocks covering 47,058 square kilometres were subsequently offered in the Andaman basin under OALP-X.ONGC and Oil India have taken exploration into the ultra-deepwater region, with drilling operations targeting depths of up to 5,000 metres.One important well is ONGC's ANDW-7 in the East Andaman Back Arc region. The well encountered traces of light crude and condensate in cutting samples, C-5 neo-pentane in trip gases and reservoir-quality facies. The government said the findings provided evidence of an active thermogenic petroleum system in the region, comparable with petroleum systems in Myanmar and North Sumatra.The findings do not establish a commercially producing field. The government has said commercial reserves in the Andaman campaign remain to be established. Their significance lies in providing evidence of a working petroleum system that can guide further exploration.The Krishna-Godavari basin off India's eastern coast is a more established offshore hydrocarbon province but remains central to the country's deepwater strategy.In OALP Round VIII, the 2022 KG-UDWHP-2022/1 ultra-deepwater block in the Krishna-Godavari basin covered 1,199.64 square kilometres. This was the size of that particular block, not the total current exploration acreage of the basin.The Krishna-Godavari basin has also attracted international technical collaboration. In 2022, ONGC signed a Heads of Agreement with ExxonMobil for deepwater exploration covering the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins on the eastern coast and the Kutch-Mumbai region on the western coast.The Cauvery Offshore Basin is another important part of India's eastern offshore exploration map.The government's 2026 Samudra Manthan backgrounder cites recent finds in the Cauvery, Mahanadi and Andaman basins as evidence supporting the broader offshore opportunity.The basin is part of India's wider effort to identify additional offshore resources through deeper and more technically demanding exploration.Samudra Manthan is not confined to India's eastern coast. The western offshore belt, including Kutch and Mumbai Offshore, is also part of the country's wider exploration strategy.The government has identified Mahanadi and Kutch as areas where common offshore infrastructure is particularly important because high production and evacuation costs can prevent discoveries from moving into production.OALP Round VIII in 2022 included blocks in Mumbai Offshore, Kutch, Saurashtra and Kerala-Konkan. ONGC's collaboration with ExxonMobil also covered the Kutch-Mumbai region, keeping the western offshore belt within India's broader deepwater exploration push.The numbers attached to Samudra Manthan describe a large opportunity, but they do not mean India already has 5,600 MMTOE of proven offshore reserves waiting to be produced.The government estimates more than 5,600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon potential across India's eastern and western offshore basins. Separately, subject to exploration success, Samudra Manthan aims to add more than 600 MMTOE of hydrocarbon reserves, expand the country's hydrocarbon resource base from 1.6 billion tonnes of oil equivalent to 2.2 billion tonnes of oil equivalent, and increase annual domestic oil and gas production from around 62 MMTOE to 80 MMTOE.The government says the additional production could eventually reduce crude oil imports by nearly ₹1 lakh crore a year.The distinction between potential, reserves and production is critical. Seismic surveys identify promising geological structures, but drilling is required to establish whether hydrocarbons are actually present. A discovery then needs appraisal, reserve estimation and commercial assessment before it can move into development and production.Samudra Manthan therefore goes beyond drilling. Its ₹84,084 crore framework combines geological data acquisition, deepwater drilling support, common infrastructure, and domestic manufacturing and services capacity.The immediate picture is spread across different stages. Mahanadi is in an appraisal campaign designed to evaluate hydrocarbon discoveries. Andaman remains a frontier basin where geological evidence points to an active petroleum system, but commercial reserves have yet to be established. Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery remain important eastern offshore targets for deeper exploration, while Kutch and other western offshore areas form part of the wider exploration and infrastructure strategy.Samudra Manthan is therefore not simply India's ₹84,084 crore plan to drill more wells. It is the latest stage of a decade-long effort to open offshore acreage, improve geological data, encourage exploration and build the infrastructure needed to bring commercially viable discoveries into production.The decisive test will be whether prospects beneath the Mahanadi, Andaman, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and other offshore areas can make the journey from geological potential to commercially recoverable reserves and, finally, to actual oil and gas production in India.
Article Summary: India is taking its search for oil and natural gas deeper into the sea. The focus is now spread across the Mahanadi basin off Odisha, the frontier waters of the Andaman-Nicobar region, and deeper sections of the Krishna-Godavari and Cauvery basins. Prime Minister Narendra Modi gave the next phase a mission-mode identity in his Independence Day address on August 15, 2025.

Article Title: Punjab CM Mann says Rs 1,262 crore Satkar Rashi released to 36.87 lakh women
Article Text:
Punjab CM Mann says Rs 1,262 crore Satkar Rashi released to 36.87 lakh women.

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Thursday said Rs 1,262.54 crore was being transferred directly into the bank accounts of 36.87 lakh women under the state government’s Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojna.The amount constitutes the second instalment under the scheme and covers October, November and December, Mann said while addressing a function at Khandoor Sahib. Each beneficiary would receive the three-month instalment together, he said.According to Mann, Rs 2,562.33 crore had previously been distributed among 73.99 lakh women. With the latest disbursement, the total amount transferred under the scheme has reached Rs 3,824.87 crore, he said.Mann said around 97% of women in Punjab would be eligible for the scheme and that the government had set a target of extending its benefits to one crore women. He also said there were no conditions limiting the number of eligible women in a household, meaning that if three women in a family qualified, all three could receive the assistance.The chief minister said 1.37 lakh Satkar Sakhis had helped register women under the scheme and had received more than Rs 51 crore in incentives.Anganwadi workers involved in facilitating registrations would also receive incentives totalling Rs 25 crore, he said.At the event, Mann also criticised opposition parties and said that if the Congress, BJP or Akali Dal came to power, schemes including the Satkar Yojna, free bus travel for women and free electricity would be discontinued. These were political claims made by the chief minister.Mann also targeted the Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal, commenting on their internal political situation. He said the Congress had fewer workers but more leaders aspiring to become chief minister and alleged that the Akali Dal had misused religion.Referring to the state government's performance since 2022, Mann claimed that Punjab had moved from 27th to first position in school education according to the Centre's assessment. He said the government had established smart classrooms, trained teachers and recruited non-teaching staff.On medical education, Mann said around 30 lakh students appear for NEET every year and claimed that the number of students from Punjab's government schools clearing the examination had risen from 80 when he took office to 882 this year. He said the state had introduced free coaching for government-school students.Mann also said the government would open new centres for UPSC preparation to help students from Punjab prepare for the civil services.On power supply, the chief minister said eligible households were receiving 300 units of free electricity each month. He also said the state government had purchased the Goindwal Sahib Thermal Power Plant for Rs 1,080 crore.Mann said farmers were receiving daytime electricity for agricultural use and claimed that 14,000 kilometres of pipelines had been laid to take canal water to fields.He also said the pace of development in Punjab would increase between 2027 and 2032 as projects undertaken during the current government's tenure begin to show results.Cabinet minister Harbhajan Singh ETO and others were present at the event.
Article Summary: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann said Rs 1,262.54 crore was being transferred directly into the bank accounts of 36.87 lakh women. The amount constitutes the second instalment under the scheme and covers October, November and December. Mann said around 97% of women in Punjab would be eligible.

Article Title: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges fail to comply with NMC disability-unit directive

NEW DELHI: Nearly half of India’s medical colleges (44.5%) have failed to set up Enabling Units mandated by the National Medical Commission for students with benchmark disabilities. Of 798 colleges, 355 remain non-compliant, with several naming sanitation inspectors, residents, tutors and head clerks as single points of contact, according to an affidavit filed by the Commission in the Supreme Court on Tuesday.At Maharashtra Government Medical College, Nandurbar, a sanitation inspector, has been designated as the coordinator of the Enabling Unit. Other colleges have named residents, tutors and head clerks as points of contact.Dr Satendra Singh, disability-rights activist and doctor associated with Doctors with Disabilities: Agents of Change, questioned the choice of personnel for the role. “It’s unheard of for a sanitation inspector or head clerk to be made in-charge of such a committee in a medical college. They have neither the designated administrative or academic responsibility for undergraduate or postgraduate training nor the training or authority to deal with disability accommodation, clinical training, patient safety or assessment.He added, “They cannot take or escalate decisions on postings, duty hours, assistive devices, accessible infrastructure, examination accommodations or clinical-rotation modifications. Tutors and residents are also a floating population, often at an institution for only a limited period. How would a postgraduate student in pharmacology, who may not even be an alumnus of that institution, know what assistance a wheelchair-using medical student needs in an operation theatre or have the authority to direct the theatre staff?”The NMC circular does not prescribe a doctor or clinical faculty member as the single point of contact. It does, however, assign the Enabling Unit responsibility for reasonable accommodation, academic and clinical support, barrier-free access, coordination, record-keeping and information dissemination.The compliance exercise was undertaken following the Supreme Court’s August 4, 2026 order in Anmol vs Union of India, which directed the NMC to seek college-wise compliance with its July 27 circular through Deans and Principals.The court warned that if colleges failed to respond or follow the directions, “a serious view will be taken against the individual colleges.”The NMC’s affidavit said 515 of 798 colleges had responded by September 28: 443 reported full compliance, 26 partial or ongoing compliance, and 46 submitted only the committee-constitution order. As many as 283 colleges did not respond. Majority of NMC-designated medical assessment boards and appellate boards themselves fail to comply, despite NMC warning that “serious view” would be takenThe commission had set September 10 as the deadline and issued reminders on September 23 and 24, the latter warning that late submissions would not be accepted and show-cause notices would follow. Colleges were required to provide details of the unit, its members and POC, functionality, accessibility, communication to students, records and compliance status.

At Maharashtra Government Medical College, Nandurbar, a sanitation inspector has been designated as the coordinator of the Enabling Unit.

Five Indian nationals aboard a Kuwait-flagged crude oil tanker were safely rescued after the vessel was struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the Indian embassy in Oman said on Friday.The Indian nationals were aboard MT Kazimah III, which was hit while sailing through the strategic waterway. Of these, 163 were on 12 active cargo ships, including six India-flagged vessels and six foreign-flagged vessels carrying cargo to India.“At this point, we have six India-flagged commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf. We also have six foreign-flagged vessels which are carrying cargo to India. So 12 ships are there. On these ships, we have around 163 Indian seafarers who are on board,” Jaiswal said during a media briefing.“Apart from this, we also have over 4,500 Indian seafarers who are on board various commercial vessels which are operating in the area,” he added.Jaiswal said the ministry of shipping was coordinating with Indian diplomatic missions and local stakeholders to track vessel movements and monitor the welfare of Indian seafarers.“Our ministry of shipping continues to monitor the movement of these ships and is looking at the well-being of all these seafarers, and as and when required, through our embassies and other stakeholders, they do the needful for their well-being and welfare,” he stated.“On our side, we remain committed to the safety and well-being of our seafaring community abroad,” Jaiswal said.The incident comes amid growing risks to commercial shipping across the Persian Gulf, Red Sea and Black Sea, where vessels have faced repeated attacks.External affairs minister S Jaishankar had raised concerns over attacks on commercial vessels and seafarers during his address to the 81st United Nations general assembly last week.“New challenges in the maritime domain have added to longstanding ones on land. Article Title: From papads to pitches: NCERT brings startup lessons to Class IX

NEW DELHI: Seven women, Rs 80 in borrowed capital and a Mumbai terrace. That was how Lijjat Papad began in 1959. More than six decades later, the story will be used to teach Class IX students how an idea, however small, can grow into an enterprise.NCERT’s new social science textbook has introduced a dedicated chapter on startups and entrepreneurship, taking students through the basics of identifying business opportunities, understanding markets and preparing a workable business plan.The chapter is built around three broad questions — how entrepreneurship affects society and the economy, what the main functional areas of a business are, and how an effective business plan is prepared.It also places these lessons in the context of India’s startup journey. The book says the country had only around 350-400 startups about a decade ago, while the ecosystem has now expanded to nearly 2.3 lakh enterprises, making India the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. The broader policy push, it says, is to bring research, industry, startups and entrepreneurship onto a common platform.Students are introduced to the building blocks of running a business — understanding market activity, spotting opportunities, assessing performance and planning before committing resources.The chapter also brings artificial intelligence into the discussion, explaining how AI can assist in market analysis and business decision-making.Alongside contemporary startup concepts, the book uses stories of Indian entrepreneurs to make the subject relatable.One of them is Mohan Singh Oberoi, who began his working life on a salary of Rs 50 and went on to become a pioneering figure in India’s hospitality industry. Born in Punjab in 1898, Oberoi mortgaged his wife’s jewellery to buy his first hotel and later built a major hotel business.The Lijjat Papad story, meanwhile, illustrates entrepreneurship at the other end of the scale. Seven homemakers living in a Mumbai chawl started making papads with borrowed supplies and a traditional recipe. With no factory, each woman took dough home in the morning, rolled papads while managing household work and returned the finished product by evening.The lesson highlights how quality, organisation and persistence helped turn the modest venture into a widely recognised brand.

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has busted an alleged India-Dubai extortion network linked to the Goldy Brar gang and arrested three operatives, foiling a plan to open fire at the residence of a Delhi businessman, news agency PTI reported citing officials said on Friday.The accused allegedly contacted businessman Praveen Jain through a UAE-based number on September 16 and demanded Rs 1 crore, while threatening his family with dire consequences. A case was registered at Roop Nagar police station on September 17.Police said analysis of the communication trail showed that the calls were routed through virtual private server and data-centre infrastructure linked to the UAE.The investigation led police to Aarif alias Pistol, 32, who allegedly acted as a link between the Dubai-based callers and their associates in India. He was arrested from Ahmedabad's Vejalpur on September 24 with Gujarat Police's assistance.According to police, Aarif allegedly paid a Dubai-based associate, Aarish, to make the extortion call and instructed him to speak in Haryanvi to make it appear that the threat came from a local criminal.Police subsequently arrested Mubarik alias Gullu from Delhi on September 25. Preventive arrangements were made at the house, foiling the alleged attack.During the probe, police found that the same UAE number was allegedly used to target another Delhi businessman in Rohini. Investigators are examining communication records, digital evidence and financial transactions to establish the wider network and determine whether the group was involved in other extortion cases.

NEW DELHI: RSS leader Ramlal described the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh’s first national conference of women farmers as a symbol of women’s growing role in Indian agriculture and a platform to advocate changes in agricultural policies, according to the PTI report.Speaking at the event, RSS All-India Sampark Pramukh Ramlal said around 5,000 women farmers and office-bearers from across the country, including states such as Arunachal Pradesh and Manipur, travelled to Delhi at their own expense to participate in the All India Women Farmers’ Workers Conclave held at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium on Wednesday.RSS leader Ramlal, who attended the conference, said women farmers should have a central role in decision-making on issues related to sustainable agriculture and the development of rural economies.In a statement, the RSS All-India Sampark Pramukh said "women should receive legal and social recognition not just as agricultural workers but as farmers and agricultural entrepreneurs capable of making independent decisions with self reliance and discernment."He congratulated the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh (BKS) for highlighting women’s empowerment and called on other organisations to draw lessons from such efforts.Ramlal said the women who travelled to Delhi at their own expense and raised the slogan, “We, the women of India, will bring prosperity”, had added a new sense of pride and dignity to the term “Annadata” (food provider). He said their participation could mark the beginning of a significant transformation towards a healthier and more prosperous future for the country.He noted that women have traditionally played an important role in Indian agriculture, from sowing and harvesting crops to preserving indigenous seeds and rearing livestock.According to Ramlal, women perform nearly 60 to 70 per cent of the physical work associated with agriculture. However, he said they have often been classified in society and official records merely as agricultural labourers or family helpers.The conference, organised under the guidance of the women’s wing of the Bharatiya Kisan Sangh, sought to change this perception and ensure women farmers receive recognition, dignity and self-respect, he said.Ramlal said the event, held against the backdrop of the United Nations’ declaration of 2026 as the “International Year of the Woman Farmer”, was more than an organisational gathering but it was more of a manifestation of the women empowerment in Indian agriculture. He described it and a call for changes in agricultural policies.He said participants discussed the role of traditional farming in achieving the vision of a developed and healthy India by 2047, with “Gau-Krishi-Vanijyam” (cattle, agriculture and commerce) also featuring in the deliberations.Opposition to genetically modified (GM) seeds and gene-editing technology was another key issue discussed at the conference, Ramlal said.The conference identified five key areas: toxin-free farming and cow-based organic agriculture, nutritious food, disease-free living, an addiction-free society and remunerative prices for agricultural produce, he said.Ramlal also urged the Centre and state governments to put women farmers at the centre of policymaking and design schemes according to their requirements. He called for easier access to credit, local processing facilities and better avenues for marketing organic products.He said existing policies often focus on corporate and chemical-based farming, while arguing that women’s participation is crucial to rural development.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people. It can also reduce the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, according to an IARC assessment. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's $200 million Six Flags investment faces new low as investors push for a potential sale

Article Title: UPI transactions rise 27% to 145 billion in H1 FY27 ahead of new MDR
Article Text:
UPI transactions rise 27%

New MDR regime starts October 15

Everyday UPI payments to remain free

Pay via UPI in 11 countries

UPI's digital tap-to-pay habit appears to be getting stronger by the month. The platform processed around 145 billion transactions in the first half of the current financial year, up 27% from 114 billion in the same period last year, according to National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) data.The value of those transactions rose at a slightly slower clip, climbing 20% to Rs 177 lakh crore from Rs 148 lakh crore a year earlier.However, September numbers showed a marginal month-on-month decline in both UPI volume and value. During the month, transaction volume stood at 24.07 billion, down 1.7% from 24.5 billion in August. The value of transactions fell 1.5% to Rs 29.37 lakh crore from Rs 29.82 lakh crore in the previous month.The monthly decline, however, needs to be viewed in the context of the difference in the number of days in the two months. August had 31 days, compared with 30 in September. Industry watchers pointed out that despite the lower monthly numbers, the average daily transactions were higher in September at 802 million, against 791 million in August.The September data comes just two weeks before the implementation of a new merchant discount rate (MDR) on specified high-value UPI payments.From October 15, merchants will be charged an MDR of 0.4% on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000. The charge will apply to merchant payments and not person-to-person transactions, which will remain free irrespective of the amount involved.The new MDR framework is aimed at creating a sustainable revenue model for the digital payments ecosystem. MDR is the fee merchants pay to payment service providers for processing digital transactions.The amount collected through the MDR will be distributed across the UPI ecosystem. Customers' banks will receive 40% of the MDR, payment gateways 30%, UPI apps 20% and the sponsoring bank of the UPI app the remaining 10%, PTI reported.The charge will be paid by merchants rather than consumers and will be capped at Rs 300 for transactions of Rs 75,000 or more.The new charge will not apply to person-to-person payments. The vast majority of everyday merchant transactions will also continue to remain free.A separate fee structure has been set for certain essential services. Transactions above Rs 2,000 involving railways, telecom, fuel and insurance will attract a flat Rs 5 fee per transaction.For capital market transactions, including mutual funds and stockbroking, the MDR will be 0.02%, subject to a cap of Rs 300.Small merchants will also remain outside the new charge if they collect up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR codes. This exemption covers about 96% of all merchant transactions.UPI's reach has also extended beyond India, with the payment system now accepted in 11 countries. Uzbekistan is the latest addition to the list. UPI is also accepted in Singapore, the United Arab Emirates, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Bhutan, Qatar, Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Greece.NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), operates as the umbrella organisation for retail payments and settlement systems in India. It runs UPI, which enables real-time payments between individuals as well as payments to merchants.Since its launch on August 25, 2016, UPI has seen a sharp rise in transaction value. Transactions worth Rs 0.07 lakh crore were recorded through the system in FY17. By FY26, the figure had risen to around Rs 314 lakh crore, an increase of more than 4,000 times over the decade.
Article Summary: UPI processed 145 billion transactions in the first half of the current financial year, up 27% from 114 billion in the same period last year. September numbers showed a marginal month-on-month decline in both UPI volume and value. Data comes two weeks before the implementation of a new merchant discount rate (MDR) on specified high-value UPI payments.

Article Title: A year on, Bengaluru-Mumbai superfast train promise remains on paper
Article Text:
Despite a promise made a year ago by the Railway Minister, no superfast train service exists between Bengaluru and Mumbai

TOI





BENGALURU: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters for years.On Sept 27, 2025, Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya announced through his X account that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had assured him of a superfast train connecting the two cities. Twelve months later, however, the promised train has not started.For passengers, the situation has changed little. For over three decades, Udyan Express has remained the only daily direct service between Bengaluru and Mumbai that takes roughly 24 hours to cover the journey.There was some movement in May 2026, when railways introduced a bi-weekly SMVT Bengaluru-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express. But the additional service did not address the central demand for a faster connection: that train too takes around 24 hours.The next assurance raised expectations further. In May, Vaishnaw tolda Vande Bharat sleeper service on Bengaluru-Mumbai route will be introduced in Aug. That, too, has not materialised.The railway board subsequently allocated a rake that had initially been planned for Bengaluru-Mumbai route to Northern Railway zone, leaving passengers without a launch date for the proposed service.Rail users from across Karnataka have taken to social media to question the delay. Karnataka Rail Users sarcastically marked the first anniversary of the announcement, while other passenger groups accused the Centre and South Western Railway (SWR) zone of making promises without delivering the service.Mahendra Singhi, a member of SWR’s Zonal Railway Users’ Consultative Committee in Hubballi, said the railway board should introduce a Vande Bharat on the route to provide the speed and comfort passengers have been seeking.The BJP’s Karnataka migrant outreach network has also sought an early decision. “Nearly a year has passed since the announcement, yet there has been no official communication regarding the launch date of this service. The train will significantly benefit passengers and strengthen connectivity between Bengaluru, the IT capital of India, and Mumbai, the financial capital,“ Bharat Jain, co-convener (Karnataka), BJP Rajasthani Pravasi Prakoshth, stated.
Article Summary: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion. It plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses.

Article Title: RBI rate hikes ahead? BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027
Article Text:
BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise interest rates by 100 basis points through the first half of 2027, according to Bank of America (BofA) Securities. The brokerage has also moved up its estimate for the first rate hike, now expecting the hike in October instead of December.BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.The new forecast is twice the size of BofA's earlier 50 basis point estimate.“Our bigger forecast shift is arguably the quantum of hikes, as we are raising our total quantum of hikes from 50bp earlier, to 100bp now,” BofA said.BofA expects the RBI to raise rates by 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of 2026 and another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027. It also expects the central bank to change its monetary policy stance in December.“The RBI will switch the stance in December to one of calibrated tightening”, the report said.So, what has changed in BofA's view? The brokerage said the domestic economy remains resilient, giving the RBI less reason to wait before raising rates.At the same time, inflation risks are becoming broader.Oil prices remained around $100-110 per barrel for most of September, BofA said. It also pointed to rising risks of fuel price increases and food-related supply pressures.Strong economic growth is another factor behind the revised outlook. BofA said the strength of the economy is reducing the need for the RBI to keep monetary conditions accommodative.Non-food credit growth stood at 17.8 per cent year-on-year in September, while investment demand is expected to remain healthy in the second quarter of FY27.Inflation pressures are also spreading, according to the report. BofA said food inflation is becoming more broad-based, while wholesale inflation is increasingly spreading to other sectors. Tradables inflation rose to 5.9 per cent in August 2026.The brokerage has also laid out a scenario in which the RBI could go beyond the 100-basis-point increase it currently expects. If real GDP growth stays around 7 per cent and headline inflation remains close to 5.5 per cent, BofA said the central bank could raise rates by more than 100 basis points.In that case, front-end rates could rise above 6.5 per cent, the brokerage said.But a sharp slowdown in growth could change the rate outlook. BofA said the RBI could deliver fewer hikes or no hike if growth falls below 7 per cent and moves towards 6 per cent on a forward-looking basis.
Article Summary: Bank of America Securities sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027. BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.

Article Title: 90% of dementia cases in TN go undiagnosed: State turns focus to early screening and care
Article Text:
About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia (AI Image)





CHENNAI: With more than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed, the state is looking at making the condition a “public health priority”.“Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. The number of people with dementia is projected to double to 10 lakh,” says Ramani Sundaram of Dementia India Alliance (DIA), which recently organised DemCon in Chennai, a conference on the condition.DIA is a national organisation focused on dementia awareness, care, support and brain healthAt DemCon, state health minister K G Arunraj said the govt would work towards a “coordinated state plan”. “The MoU between the department of health and family welfare and DIA is an important step in this direction,” said Arun Raj. “This partnership is an expression of our shared commitment to strengthening dementia care.”The state plan will look at standardising screening, assessment, referral and treatment, as well as making diagnosis, systematic referrals and follow-up part of the existing primary healthcare infrastructure.“It’s important to create awareness as dementia care costs about Rs 3 lakh per person annually, apart from the informal cost of care provided by family members,” says Ramani. “Cognitive impairment cannot be reduced to simply asking an elderly person whether they are becoming forgetful. ”An ongoing screening programme conducted since Feb by DIA in collaboration with the state govt among 2,500 elderly people in Coimbatore, Erode and Chengalpet, found 9% had cognitive impairment.Among those screened, 30% reported neurological problems such as slowness, tremors, falls or limb weakness, while 28% had sleep disturbances. About 27% reported feeling sad, irritable, or disinterested in their usual activities, while 18% had trouble with memory, wayfinding or planning. About 12% had difficulty speaking, understanding, naming, reading or writing, and 7% said they heard voices or saw images when alone.About 35% of those screened had hypertension, which, says Ramani, is among the risk factors for dementia. “There was substance abuse in about 15% of those screened, while a large percentage – 42 – chewed tobacco. These are also among the risk factors. Up to 45% of dementia can be prevented if these are addressed. So, this is an important part of the action plan to make Tamil Nadu a dementia-aware state,” says Ramani.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu has a rapidly ageing population. People over 60 make up 16% of the population in 2026, and it is projected to reach 20% in 10 years. More than five lakh people in Tamil Nadu living with dementia, and 90% believed to be undiagnosed. The state is looking at making the condition a ‘public health priority’
